en.correct: the tensile stress that develops at an angle within a beam's web due to the combination of shear and bending, often governing shear crack orientation

the compressive stress that develops along the top fiber of a bent beam

example.text: Diagonal tension cracks near the beam's support indicated the stirrups were being called on to resist the shear.

en.correct: a localized failure of a thin beam web caused by concentrated bearing forces crushing or buckling the material near a support or load point
distractors: the overall lateral buckling of an entire unbraced beam
the fatigue cracking of a beam's flange after repeated cyclic loading

example.text: Without a stiffener at the reaction point, the thin steel web was vulnerable to web crippling under the concentrated load.

the vertical sagging of a beam caused purely by excessive deflection

example.text: The long unbraced steel beam had to be checked for lateral torsional buckling before it reached its full bending capacity.

en.correct: the buckling of a thin individual plate element, such as a flange or web, within a larger structural member, occurring before the whole member buckles

the buckling of a bracing system connecting multiple structural frames

example.text: The thin-walled steel section was classified as slender because local buckling of its flanges could occur before it reached yield.

en.correct: a beam made of two different materials, typically steel and concrete, connected to act together as a single structural unit

a beam that spans continuously over more than two supports

example.text: The composite beam combined a rolled steel section with a concrete slab connected by shear studs to increase its stiffness.

a reinforcing bar bent to anchor a slab into a supporting wall

example.text: Rows of shear studs were welded along the beam flange before the concrete deck was poured over it.

en.correct: a steel plate placed beneath a beam, column, or truss to spread a concentrated load over a wider area of the supporting material

a decorative cover plate hiding an exposed steel connection

a foundation system designed specifically to resist overturning moments

a foundation system reinforced with diagonal steel piles

a foundation grid of intersecting grade beams beneath a slab

a diagonal brace placed only within the building's central core

a temporary truss used to support formwork during a slab pour

a hydraulic jack used to level a settling structure after construction

a rubber bearing that isolates a structure from ground motion

a hydraulic bearing that actively adjusts a structure's elevation

a bearing formed from stacked timber blocks used only on temporary structures

a bearing consisting of layered rubber sheets bonded to steel plates

a temporary cable used only to hold a segment in place during erection

en.correct: the curve naturally formed by a flexible cable or chain hanging freely under its own weight between two supports

the parabolic curve a projectile follows under gravity alone

the line along which reinforcing steel is placed in a concrete arch

en.correct: a local thickening or deepening of a beam or slab near a support, added to increase its capacity to resist bending and shear

a temporary wedge used to adjust formwork alignment before a pour

a groove cut into a slab to control the location of shrinkage cracks

the horizontal displacement of a retaining wall measured after construction

the twisting of a member about its longitudinal axis under torsion

en.correct: a bending condition in which a structural member curves downward at midspan, producing tension in the bottom fiber
distractors: a bending condition that produces tension in the top fiber over a support
the lateral buckling of a beam under axial compression

en.correct: the location along a bent structural member where the bending moment changes sign from positive to negative, or vice versa

the location where a column's axial load is applied eccentrically

the bending moment that causes complete flexural failure of a member

an impermeable synthetic liner used to contain contaminated groundwater

a rigid plastic grid used to reinforce weak soil under a road

distractors: a treatment that fully waterproofs a wall against standing groundwater pressure
an admixture added to concrete to reduce its water-cement ratio

a sealant bead applied along the top edge of a curtain wall panel

an opening left in a foundation purely to route electrical conduit

a zone of dry soil found directly beneath an otherwise saturated layer

the pressure generated by a pump used to dewater an excavation

the lateral pressure exerted by saturated soil against a basement wall

an instrument used to measure groundwater pressure at depth

a sealed enclosure used to keep water out of a deep excavation

a vertical steel pile driven to retain the face of an excavation

en.correct: a structural member that resists compressive force, often used to brace an excavation, truss, or frame between two points

a flexible cable used to hang a suspended floor from a roof truss

en.correct: an inclined strut used to brace a retaining wall or excavation face, typically bearing against a foundation or pile at its lower end

a vertical pile driven purely to support a crane's outrigger

the resistance a pile's tip provides when bearing directly on rock

the lateral force imposed on a pile by an adjacent excavation

a horizontal beam cast into a wall to distribute vertical load

a driven steel pile used to support a building's foundation

a bolt used to anchor equipment to a finished concrete floor

the ventilation duct system installed along a tunnel's length

the vertical shaft used to access a tunnel from the surface

the settlement of ground above a tunnel after excavation passes

to waterproof the exterior of a foundation wall

to compact loose soil using a vibratory plate

for a foundation to settle unevenly under a building's weight

example.text: The garage's concrete columns had begun to spall wherever the reinforcing steel underneath was rusting.

distractors: to add water to a dry soil sample before compaction testing
to flush contaminated water out of a completed drainage pipe

describing a material that fully recovers its original shape once unloaded
